subject.title: fix(gateway): force exit on zombie shutdown + 503 healthz during shutdown

question: After moving failed-startup forced exit to the terminal process owner, should Gateway retain a separate post-close watchdog and configurable timeout as a permanent lifecycle contract?
rationale: The blocking ownership defect is mechanical, but permanent process-exit ownership and a new operator environment surface require explicit lifecycle and product intent.

options.title: Process owner, internal timeout
options.body: Arm the watchdog only from terminal CLI or daemon paths and keep its timeout as an internal implementation constant.

options.title: Process owner, documented config
options.body: Move ownership to the terminal path and explicitly support and document the environment timeout.

options.title: Extend the existing timer
options.body: Cover the zombie gap through the current CLI force-exit policy instead of maintaining a second watchdog.

recommendation.title: Process owner, internal timeout
recommendation.body: Arm the watchdog only from terminal CLI or daemon paths and keep its timeout as an internal implementation constant.

likelyOwner.reason: Current history connects this person to both the existing Gateway process-exit policy and the recoverable onboarding caller affected by the decision.
